leads.title: Salvarsan and synthetic antimicrobial drugs
leads.why: Screening hundreds of made compounds against syphilis produced the first targeted synthetic cure and the method that led to the sulfonamides.
leads.verify: The dates of Ehrlich and Hata's tests of compound 606 and its 1910 release; Ehrlich's earlier dye-based work; the link to Prontosil (1935).
search: history of chemotherapy Ehrlich magic bullet

leads.title: Written medicine in Mesopotamia
leads.where: Southern Mesopotamia (Nippur, later Babylon and Nineveh)
leads.date: c. 2100 BCE (earliest medical tablet); diagnostic handbook c. 1050 BCE
leads.why: Healers recorded remedies and a symptom-by-symptom diagnostic handbook that scribal schools copied for two thousand years.
leads.verify: The date, findspot and contents of the oldest medical tablet (the Ur III tablet from Nippur); the date and authorship of the diagnostic series Sakikku attributed to Esagil-kin-apli; the roles of the asu and the asipu; whether any content passed to Egypt or Greece.
search: oldest Sumerian medical tablet Nippur Ur III pharmacopoeia

leads.title: Written medicine in pharaonic Egypt
leads.date: physicians attested from c. 2650 BCE; earliest surviving medical papyrus c. 1825 BCE
leads.why: Titled physicians worked from papyri of case descriptions, wound treatment and several hundred remedies, and Greek writers later drew on Egyptian drugs.
leads.verify: The earliest securely dated physician title and the dates of the Kahun, Edwin Smith and Ebers papyri (and of the older texts they copy); the evidence for independence from Mesopotamian medicine; what demonstrably passed to Greek medicine.
search: Edwin Smith papyrus date surgical cases
ancient Egyptian physicians swnw earliest attestation

leads.title: Hippocratic medicine in Greece
leads.where: Kos, Knidos and the Aegean Greek cities
leads.why: Greek physicians wrote case histories and explained illness by natural causes, and through Galen this medicine governed practice in Europe and the Islamic world for two millennia.
leads.verify: The dating of the earliest treatises in the Hippocratic Corpus; how much Greek medicine took from Egyptian and Mesopotamian practice, which scholars dispute; the route into Roman, Syriac and Arabic medicine.
search: Egyptian Mesopotamian influence on Greek medicine

leads.title: The bimaristan teaching hospital
leads.why: Endowed city hospitals with wards, salaried physicians, pharmacies and bedside teaching made the hospital a place of medical training.
leads.verify: The earliest securely documented bimaristan in Baghdad and its founder; the debated role of Gondeshapur and of Syriac Christian hospitals as models; when wards for the insane and clinical teaching are first attested.
search: first bimaristan Baghdad Harun al-Rashid date
Dols origins of the Islamic hospital myth and reality
Pormann Savage-Smith medieval Islamic medicine hospitals

leads.title: The randomised controlled trial in British medicine
leads.where: London and Medical Research Council hospitals, Britain
leads.why: Random allocation gave medicine a trusted test of whether a treatment works, and drug approval everywhere now depends on it.
leads.verify: The design and publication of the 1948 streptomycin trial and Austin Bradford Hill's role; earlier controlled comparisons (James Lind's scurvy trial of 1747, alternate-allocation trials, the 1944 patulin trial) and R. A. Fisher's agricultural experiments, to state exactly what was new.

history of randomised controlled trial James Lind Library

concepts.name: Antimicrobial chemotherapy
concepts.summary: Curing an infection with a synthetic chemical designed to kill the microbe and spare the patient.

concepts.name: Hospital
concepts.summary: A permanent institution where the sick are lodged and treated by attendants and physicians.

concepts.name: Learned medicine
concepts.summary: A body of diagnosis, prognosis and remedies that specialists record, teach and hand on as a discipline.

concepts.name: Randomised controlled trial
concepts.summary: Testing a treatment by allotting patients at random to receive it or not and comparing the outcomes.
